newsitem.title: USA: COMEX broker settles with CFTC.
newsitem.headline: COMEX broker settles with CFTC.

text.p: A Commodity Exchange Inc (COMEX) floor broker agreed to pay a $75,000 fine and to stop trading on a contract market for nine months, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said Tuesday.
As part of the settlement, broker Christopher Engel also agreed to cooperate with the CFTC in any related investigations.
The CFTC issued an order accepting a settlement offer from Engel in connection with a complaint filed against him in 1993.

The CFTC order found that Engel engaged in wash sales and accommodation trading that caused the reporting of false prices. The order also found that Engel was involved in prearranged trades with another broker.
Engel, who did not admit or deny the findings in the agency's order, agreed to pay a $75,000 civil fine and to stop trading for nine months.
Commissioner John Tull dissented from the agency's acceptance of the settlement offer by Engel. ((Washington commodities desk, 202 898 8467))
